children: New Delhi, Sept. 8 -- Hazoor Multi Projects, a small-cap stock with a market capitalisation of less than Rs.1,000 crore, is likely to attract investors' attention in Wednesday's session, September 9, after the company secured a work order from the National Highways Authority of India (NHAI).
In an exchange filing aftermarket hour on Tuesday, the company said it had received a new order for user-fee collection services.
The company said it had received a Letter of Award (LOA) dated September 7, 2026, from NHAI for a user-fee collection agency contract, awarded through a competitive bidding process via e-tender.

The contract covers the Pudhupatti fee plaza at Km 39.760 of the Salem-Vayembadi section from Km 36.000 to Km 80.000 of NH-179A in Tamil Nadu. It also includes the upkeep and maintenance of adjacent toilet blocks, including the replenishment of consumable items.
The project is scheduled to be completed within 12 months from the date of commencement, while the order value stands at Rs.42 crore, according to the filing.

The company's shares have been under sustained selling pressure since hitting a fresh all-time high in September 2024, resulting in a significant erosion of shareholder wealth. From the peak of Rs.63.90, the stock has fallen to around Rs.20 apiece, translating into a 69% decline.

After ending CY25 with a 33% decline, the selling pressure continued into the current year, with the stock falling another 40% so far in 2026. The stock has ended five of the last seven months in the red, with March recording the steepest monthly decline of 27%.
The prolonged weakness has also pushed the stock to its lowest level since December 2023, a level it touched last month.
Despite the recent correction, Hazoor Multi Projects has delivered exceptional returns over the longer term.

Between April 2021 and September 2024, the small-cap stock attracted strong buying interest, surging from Rs.0.43 apiece to Rs.55.33, translating into a massive 12,767% gain. During this period, the stock also touched a fresh all-time high of Rs.63.90 apiece.

On a yearly basis, the stock delivered positive returns in five of the last six years, with three of those years qualifying as multibagger years. 2021 was its best-performing year, when the stock surged 724%, followed by gains of 373% in 2023 and 192% in 2022.

Despite the recent losses, the stock remains 50% higher over the past three years and nearly 1,200% higher over the past five years, highlighting the substantial long-term gains it has delivered despite the recent correction.
